reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, MIN(s.order_date) - p.launch_date AS days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.launch_date
alternatives:
WITH first_sales AS (  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_day
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.product_id, f.first_day - p.launch_date AS days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN first_sales f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'

SELECT p.product_id, date_diff('day', p.launch_date, MIN(s.order_date)) AS days_to_first_sale FROM products p JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.launch_date

other_way.sql:
WITH first_sales AS (  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_day
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.product_id, f.first_day - p.launch_date AS days_to_first_sale
FROM products p
JOIN first_sales f ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.launch_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
other_way.tradeoff: Finding each product's first sale in its own step makes the grain clear, but one GROUP BY does it in fewer lines.

solver.query:

FROM products p

WHERE CAST(p.launch_date AS DATE) >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.launch_date
